title: Best AI study apps for Indian students
summary: Choose between NotebookLM and Educato for Indian college coursework, from bilingual lecture notes to phone revision and written answers.
body_markdown:
Choose NotebookLM if your main problem is finding an explanation across scattered lecture material. Choose Educato if you have the material and want a routine for practising it. For an Indian college student deciding between them, the most useful thing to bring to the decision is a question from your own class that you struggled to answer.


Educato publishes this page and makes one of the apps on it. We list it where it fits, with its limits.


## Which AI study app suits Indian college students?


For a student starting with a folder of course readings, we recommend NotebookLM for making sense of the folder, then Educato for practising what it contains. Reverse that order if you already understand the readings but draw a blank when the paper asks you to apply them.


1. **NotebookLM, best for studying across sources.** You can ask about the material in a notebook or turn sources into flashcards, slides and audio overviews. A personal Gmail account gives you access to notebooks. The trade-off is that you still have to decide which parts of a reading deserve practice and whether you can explain them without the overview.
2. **Educato, best for fitting practice from your notes into a daily plan.** Its own-material options include PDFs, slide decks, Word documents and photos of notes. Flashcards, explanations and a daily plan suit a student who needs another encounter with yesterday's difficult topic. **Limits.** Full access is paid, and AI-generated explanations can contain mistakes. A tidy plan cannot tell whether your folder includes everything your lecturer assigned.


Option Details Source


NotebookLM Users can turn sources into flashcards, slide decks and audio or video overviews. Google AI Plus and Pro raise the number of notebooks and sources allowed.[Source](https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/16213268?hl=en) (checked 2026-11-27)


NotebookLM The mobile app supports questions about notebook sources and offline listening to downloaded Audio Overviews.[Source](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.google.android.apps.labs.language.tailwind) (checked 2026-11-27)


NotebookLM A personal Gmail account can open 100 notebooks and add up to 50 sources per notebook, excluding notes from that source limit.[Source](https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/16213268?hl=en) (checked 2026-11-27)


The product descriptions come from[Google's notebook help](https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/16213268?hl=en) and[Educato's study page](https://www.educato.com/) , checked on 27 November 2026. The order above reflects those published features. Your course, the kind of work you hand in and the device you usually have with you should decide the rest.


### Try a question from your last internal assessment


Suppose an economics lecturer asks why a fall in the price of tea differs from a change in people's taste for tea. The relevant notes contain a demand diagram and a paragraph about changes in demand. An app can produce a smooth summary of both and still leave you unable to draw the right picture. Start with a blank page. Draw what you think happens in each case. Put a question mark beside the part you cannot justify.


If the uncertainty is over the meaning of an axis or the lecturer's use of “other things equal”, open the source alongside the notebook and ask where that condition enters the explanation. Go back to the paragraph and read the sentence on either side. If you understand the distinction when you see the graph but keep reversing the cases from memory, make that distinction the subject of your next practice session. Check the prediction you drew. A fall in the price of tea moves the point along the existing demand curve. If buyers develop a stronger taste for tea, they want more at the same price, so you need a second curve. Label the price you held fixed and mark the two quantities. Change tea to a different good and draw the diagram again before looking at the answer.


### Keep class vocabulary when your notes mix languages


You might discuss a concept in Hindi, Marathi or Tamil while the slides and answer script use English terminology. Keep the term from the slide next to the phrase that helped you understand it. If an app substitutes another English term, check whether your lecturer uses those words interchangeably. A translation can read naturally while quietly changing the distinction the question is testing.


Make yourself explain the idea aloud in the language you use with classmates. Then write the answer in the language your course expects, including the labels on any diagram. Compare the two attempts. If the reasoning works aloud but the written sentence is vague, spend your time practising that sentence. Uploading another chapter would give you more material without fixing the gap.


## Which AI study app should I choose if I mostly revise on my phone?


Choose NotebookLM for listening to a downloaded overview on the bus, or Educato for picking up practice you started on a computer. For anything that involves a diagram, try the task on the phone you actually carry. Open a page of handwritten calculations, a photograph of a board or a slide with a small labelled figure. Can you read the original while checking the answer? A beautifully formatted explanation is little help if switching back to the source loses your place every time.


For a commute, Google's[mobile listing](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.google.android.apps.labs.language.tailwind) describes offline listening to downloaded Audio Overviews. Download the overview while connected and pick a stopping point before leaving. Pause there and say the next step in the argument yourself. Save graph drawing or checking a derivation for when you have paper and can see the labels. With Educato, synced phone and web access can suit a different routine: prepare material at a computer, then return to practice on your phone.


If classmates share photographs after a lecture, test a familiar page with a diagram and a handwritten correction in the margin. Compare the correction with the file the app actually received. On a small screen you may see a perfectly readable heading while the arrow beside it has disappeared. A quiz based on that upload can then reinforce the exact mistake your lecturer corrected. Keep the clearer original or transcribe the correction before saving those questions.


### What should I check before spending money?


Write down the exact job that the free account leaves unfinished. Perhaps you need to keep several subjects apart, or perhaps you want more practice on a single unit. Those are different reasons to pay. Check what your account offers in India, the billing period and what access continues if you stop paying. A price shown to a student abroad is a poor basis for your budget.


Give the tool a fair trial with a chapter you have already studied. You know enough to spot a missing qualification, and you can compare its output with a marked answer. Keep the corrected answer, close the app and try a new version on paper the next day. If the extra practice changed what you could produce unaided, you have a concrete reason to keep using it. If all you kept was a nicer set of notes, ask whether that was the job you wanted done.
